overview: This single-page file contains an unclassified airgram from the U.S. Political Adviser in Tokyo reporting the planned establishment of radiotelephone service between Japan and Formosa (Taiwan). It reproduces a December 24, 1949, General Headquarters public-information release announcing that Japan’s Ministry of Telecommunications had received authorization to operate the circuit, expected to become available around January 1, 1950, and specifying the Japanese government’s charges for calls, overtime, and reports.

subfiles.title: Airgram on Japan–Formosa radiotelephone service
subfiles.from: U.S. Political Adviser, Tokyo (William J. Sebald)
subfiles.about: Reports the authorization, anticipated opening, and rates of a radiotelephone circuit between Japan and Formosa.
subfiles.summary: The airgram transmits a news item released on December 24, 1949, by the Public Information Office of General Headquarters, U.S. Air East Command, Tokyo. Japan’s Ministry of Telecommunications had been authorized to establish radiotelephone service with Formosa, with service expected around January 1, 1950. The announced tariff was 2,160 yen for the first three minutes, 720 yen for each additional minute or fraction thereof, and 216 yen for report charges.

interest: The document provides a concise record of the restoration or expansion of Japan’s international communications infrastructure during the final years of the Allied occupation. Its detailed tariff schedule offers useful evidence for the economic and administrative history of postwar telecommunications, while the Japan–Formosa route is especially significant given the political transformation of Taiwan and East Asia in late 1949.
